original: - L-Glutamine ([watch Dr. Rhonda vid](https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=5DVUEKrekYw&ra=m)): The absolute premier energy substrate for enterocytes and activated immune cells. It bypasses complex digestive steps, converting directly into alpha-ketoglutarate (α-KG) inside the mitochondria to power the citric acid cycle. This immediate cellular energy hit actively drives the repair of the gut mucosal barrier and prevents LPS translocation.
rewrite: - L-Glutamine ([watch Dr. Rhonda vid](https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=5DVUEKrekYw&ra=m)) is the main fuel for your enterocytes, and for your immune cells when they're activated. It doesn't have to go through the complicated digestive steps other nutrients do. Inside the mitochondria, it gets turned straight into alpha-ketoglutarate, or α-KG. The α-KG goes into the citric acid cycle, which is how the mitochondria make their energy. So your cells get that energy right away. They use it to repair the gut lining, and that keeps LPS from getting through.

original: - Butyrate & SCFAs: While the small intestine runs on glutamine, the large intestine relies on short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) like butyrate. Getting these via raw resistant starch fermentation or your home-brewed SIBO yogurt fuels colonocytes, locks down the lower gut barrier, and systematically suppresses inflammatory signals.
rewrite: - Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) like butyrate are what the colonocytes lining your large intestine rely on, instead of glutamine. You get them when your gut bacteria ferment raw resistant starch, or from your home-brewed SIBO yogurt. They feed the colonocytes, and well-fed colonocytes keep the barrier in your lower gut locked down. SCFAs also keep inflammatory signals turned down.

original: - TCA Cycle Intermediates (Malic & Citric Acid): Organic acids like malate and citrate feed directly into the exact same mitochondrial energy pathways as glutamine. Consuming clean, sour profiles—such as organic malic acid, tart cherries, or green apples—provides rapid, alternative fuel to gut epithelial cells, accelerating mucosal healing from a different biochemical angle.
rewrite: - The TCA cycle is another name for the citric acid cycle, the one glutamine feeds. Organic acids like malic and citric acid are part of that cycle, so they go directly into the same energy pathway in the mitochondria that glutamine does. That means clean sour stuff, like organic malic acid, tart cherries or green apples, gives the cells lining your gut another quick fuel. It speeds up the healing of your gut lining as well, by a different biochemical route than glutamine.
